items.title: The inclusion of adequate modules has a right adjoint
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file adequate.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For an affine scheme U = Spec(A), the lemma asserts that the inclusion of Adeq(O) into all O-modules on (Sch/U)_tau has a right adjoint, called the adequator, and that the adjunction map is an isomorphism on adequate modules (statement lines 2473-2484). The proof transfers the statement to the affine site by the big-site comparison lemma, introduces the category of module-valued functors and its adequate subcategory, refers to the chapter's construction Q as the right adjoint of the inclusion of the latter, and then displays the commutative square relating the two inclusions k and i via the functors j; defining the right adjoint as the composite Q after j, right adjointness follows from full faithfulness of j, and the isomorphism statement from full faithfulness of k (proof lines 2487-2516). The level is H3: the card's content is the assembly of the two-adjunction square, with the functors displayed in a diagram and the two formal consequences attributed to the correct full faithfulness.
